summary: Kei Kataoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (1992–2001) under Hiroshi Marui, also studying at National Sanskrit University. He held positions at Oxford, the University of Tokyo, and Kyushu University.

Keiichi Miyamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1978) under Minoru Hara. He served as an associate professor (~1986–1996) and professor (~1996–2017) at Kokugakuin University.

Keiji Nishitani was a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1921–1924) under Kitaro Nishida. He held faculty posts at Kyoto University (~1935–1963) and Otani University (~1963–1971).

Keiki Yabuki was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Tohoku Fukushi, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He taught at Shukyo University (~1913–1926), the University of Tokyo (~1924–1939), and Taisho University (~1926–1939), and founded Miwa Gakuin.

Keikyo Nakamikado is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Nakamikado was affiliated with Bukkyo University as a research collaborator in 2003 and with the Chion-in Institute of Jodo Sect Studies as a researcher in 2015.

Keir Magalie Strickland is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. Strickland completed a PhD at Durham University under the doctoral supervision of Robin Coningham (attested 2011).

Keishin Okamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1951–1956). Okamura held posts at Kōchi University (~1957–1965) and served as an associate professor at Koyasan University (~1965–1975).

Keisho Tsukamoto was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral degrees at Tohoku University. Tsukamoto served at Rissho University (~1967–1975), Hosen Gakuen College as president (~1995–2001), and Tohoku University as emeritus professor.

Keith Dowman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Bhaga Tulku, Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche, and Se Kusho Chomgpel Namgyel.

Keiya Noguchi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1980–1985). Noguchi held posts at Shuchiin University, becoming professor around 2000, and directed Taisho University's Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism.

Keizaburō Mizuno was a Japanese history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. Mizuno served at the Tokyo National Museum, Niigata Prefectural Museum of Modern Art, and Tokyo University of the Arts.

Kelsey Alise Seymour is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair. Seymour held a visiting predoctoral fellowship at the Max Planck Institute (2017–2018).

Kemu Jin was an Indology, linguistics, and Sinology scholar. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University from 1941 to 1945 and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University from around 1948 to 2000.
Kendall Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Marchman studied under Mario Poceski and earned a PhD from the University of Florida in 2015.

Keng Ching is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Harvard under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Keng served as associate professor at National Chengchi University (attested 2013–2019).

Kengo Harimoto is an Indology scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass in 1999. Harimoto has held posts at Mahidol University and the University of Naples "L'Orientale."

Kenji Matsuo is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1974 to 1985 and held a post at Yamagata University from around 1987 to 2020.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University under Peter Bisschop, with doctoral supervision also by Diwakar Acharya and Yuko Yokochi. Takahashi held a JSPS-sponsored fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II (2019–2021).
Kenji Watanabe is an Indology scholar who studied under teacher Jozef Deleu. Watanabe also held an assistant position at Taisho University, attested in 1978.

Kenjiu Kasawara was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Oxford in 1879. Kasawara studied under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell between 1879 and 1882.
